apply-canary-record._why: THE PRODUCER FOR A FILE THAT HAD ONLY CONSUMERS. The escaped `\|` matters — canary evidence contains a pipe verbatim, and an unescaped one ends the table cell.

Same tree and same arguments as apply-canary-record; the flag is the only difference and the verb changes from `would write` to `wrote`. `verified on disk:` is asserted because the confirmation RE-READS the file rather than echoing the string that was passed to write() — the defect being closed is a write that was believed and never made, so a report quoting its own input would reproduce it.

apply-deadhook-execute._why: --execute is the consent. Same tree as apply-deadhook; the only difference is the flag, and the verdict word changes from `would apply` to `applied`. Paired so a regression that makes display WRITE, or execute merely REPORT, fails one of them.

apply-emptyroot._why: wf-apply's plain (non-record-canary) DISPLAY path on a minimal root. The tree carries exactly one throwaway canary, .claude/agents/wf-canary-a.md, so PASS-STALE-CANARY has one named target; DISPLAY is the default, so the target and the --execute consent gate are printed and nothing is applied. Without a row the fixture tree was on disk and unasserted — a detector with no proof. platform-local.md carries a MEASURED-ON matching the pinned --measured-on: the third condition became a version comparison rather than a substring test (see apply-stalecanary-drifted), and this tree's record was written before there was anything to compare, so it read as unmeasured and the DISPLAY path this row exists for was never reached.

Precision is a property of the three required conditions rather than a sample, and this asserts all three by naming what must NOT appear. THE CONTROL HALF of the drift pair: platform-local.md's MEASURED-ON equals the harness version passed in, so the third condition is genuinely met and the canary is genuinely residue. --measured-on pins the comparison so the case is host-independent, exactly as it does for --record-canary.

apply-stalecanary-drifted._why: A CANARY WRITTEN TO RE-MEASURE STALE FACTS WAS SWEPT BY THE PASS THAT READS THEM. The third condition was `"TIER-LIMIT:" in platform-local.md`, a bare substring test that asks whether a measurement was ever taken and never whether it still describes the harness in the room. On a host that upgraded `claude`, the facts were stale AND the condition was green at the same time, so `--execute` deleted the fresh canary — the tier ceiling is re-measured per harness version (platform.md § Staleness), so the one moment the canary is indispensable is the moment the pass removed it. Identical tree and identical arguments to apply-stalecanary except MEASURED-ON, which is 2.1.100 here against a 2.1.223 harness: the pair isolates the verdict to that one token. REFUSED is asserted together with the reason, because a refusal whose message does not name the drift is indistinguishable from the never-measured refusal it replaced.
